home.background: I'm a full-stack developer based in Santos, Brazil, working with automation, integrations and AI agents in production. I started out studying backend on my own and got into the field through automation, where I was the technical lead of a team for almost 2 years: I talked to clients, designed the solution, built it, presented it and handled maintenance. One debt collection automation I delivered recovered around R$ 90k in about 15 days. Today I build applications with React, Next.js, Node.js, TypeScript and PostgreSQL, deploy to a VPS with Docker and keep using N8N and LLMs in my projects. I'm studying Information Systems, and before I propose any solution, I stop to understand the problem.

services.title: What I can build for you
services.subtitle: Automation, integrations and backend work for teams already feeling the cost of doing it by hand.
services.cta_title: Which process eats the most of your team's time?
services.cta_desc: Tell me how it works today. I'll tell you whether it can be automated, what access it needs, how long it takes and what it costs before you commit to anything.
services.service_1_desc: I map the process your team repeats every day and rebuild it in N8N, Make or AppScript. Triggered by webhook, spreadsheet, email or form; errors retried so one failing API doesn't stop the operation; and every run logged, so you know what went through, what failed and why.
services.service_2_desc: I get two systems that don't talk to each other exchanging data: ERP, CRM, spreadsheets, e-commerce, payment gateways. REST API or webhook with signature validation, so nobody injects a fake payload into your flow, and a queue when the volume outgrows synchronous calls. If one side goes down, the record waits in the queue instead of disappearing.
services.service_3_desc: A WhatsApp agent that answers, qualifies leads, books appointments or chases payment. It takes text, audio and images, queries your database before it replies, and keeps conversation context in Redis so it never asks the same question twice. Model output is validated before it becomes an action, so it won't invent a price or confirm an order that doesn't exist, and it hands off to a person when the conversation leaves the script.
services.service_4_desc: A Power BI or Looker Studio dashboard wired straight to the source data, with nobody exporting spreadsheets by hand every Monday. You open it and see today's number, filtered by period, with history to compare against last month.
services.service_5_desc: A Node API in TypeScript over PostgreSQL, covered by tests. Schema validation on every route that takes client input, JWT auth with hashed passwords, permissions checked on the server instead of in the UI. Split into service and repository layers, so new rules later don't break what already works. Deployed with Docker on your VPS. I've migrated 3 PostgreSQL databases from Supabase to my own VPS, with point-in-time recovery (PITR) backups using pgBackRest.
